A small $p$-value says that an estimated slope is distinguishable from zero.
It does not say that the slope is large enough to matter.
With enough data,
the standard error of $\hat\beta_1$ shrinks toward zero,
so even a tiny true slope becomes statistically significant.

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#exm-tiny-slope}
#### A statistically significant but negligible slope

We simulate $n = 10^6$ observations with

$$
\begin{aligned}
X_i &\sim \Normal(0, 1) \\
Y_i \mid X_i &\sim \Normal(0.01\, X_i,\ 1),
\end{aligned}
$$

so the true slope is $\beta_1 = 0.01$:
a one-unit increase in $X$, which is one standard deviation of $X$,
changes the mean of $Y$ by 0.01 standard deviations of $Y$'s noise.

```{r}
#| label: tiny-slope-sim
set.seed(571)
n_sim <- 1e6
beta1_true <- 0.01
x_sim <- rnorm(n_sim)
y_sim <- rnorm(n_sim, mean = beta1_true * x_sim, sd = 1)
lm_tiny <- lm(y_sim ~ x_sim)
tiny_coef <- summary(lm_tiny)$coefficients["x_sim", ]
tiny_ci <- confint(lm_tiny)["x_sim", ]
tiny_r2 <- summary(lm_tiny)$r.squared
```

The estimated slope is `r signif(tiny_coef["Estimate"], 3)`
(standard error `r signif(tiny_coef["Std. Error"], 2)`),
with a 95% confidence interval of
(`r signif(tiny_ci[1], 3)`, `r signif(tiny_ci[2], 3)`)
and $p =$ `r format.pval(tiny_coef["Pr(>|t|)"], digits = 2)`.
The test of $H_0: \beta_1 = 0$ is rejected,
yet the model explains `r signif(100 * tiny_r2, 2)`% of the variance of $Y$.
The confidence interval tells the same story:
it excludes zero, and every value in it is tiny.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#rem-signif-vs-size}
#### Significance is not importance

Statistical significance depends on the sample size
as well as on the size of the effect.
When we report a slope,
we should report the estimate and its confidence interval,
and judge whether the values in the interval are large enough to matter
in the scientific setting,
not only whether the interval excludes zero.
With $n = 10^4$ in place of $n = 10^6$,
the standard error of the same slope would be about 0.01,
so the same true slope would usually not be significant at all.
:::
